lgc_guide.text: Six thousand years of people at one lake. Neolithic farmers built rectangular houses here, some of the earliest in Ireland. Later came crannógs, artificial islands of timber and stone.
The lake was partly drained in the 1840s and the shores gave up axes, pots, bones and a great Irish elk's antlers. Every farmer had a collection on the mantelpiece.

lgc_kid.text: Did you know the lake had a goddess AND an earl in it? It's very crowded down there.
